findings.title: Unconditional visible assignment can hide groups on partial updates
findings.body: `update` always executes `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`. A PATCH or PUT that omits `visible`—including the old PATCH membership-changes API that still routes to `update` because `resources :groups` accepts PATCH—now sets `visible` to false and saves. The old `update_patch` membership add/delete handling was also removed, so such requests no longer update memberships and can silently make the group invisible. Only assign `visible` when the parameter is present, and either support or explicitly reject the old PATCH contract.

findings.title: Total page count is wrong for exact multiples
findings.body: `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. With 50 members and a 50-member page limit this reports 2 pages instead of 1, so the Next link stays enabled and takes the admin to an empty page. The same happens for 100 members (3 pages instead of 2). Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` for non-zero counts.

findings.title: Public members endpoint accepts unbounded and negative pagination values
findings.body: `limit` and `offset` are taken directly from public query parameters and passed into `.limit(...).offset(...)`. A caller can request a very large limit, causing an unnecessarily large database result and JSON serialization, or pass negative values that can produce SQL errors/500 responses. Clamp `limit` to a sane maximum and enforce `offset >= 0`.

findings.title: Public group member list truncates at 50 with no pagination
findings.body: The backend now returns only one page of members (default limit 50), and the public group-members route never requests another page. This template simply iterates `members` and has no pagination controls. Groups with more than 50 members will silently show only the first 50, whereas non-automatic groups previously returned all members. Either add paging or explicitly fetch all members for the public view.

findings.title: Removing the last member on the last page leaves an invalid offset
findings.body: `removeMember` deletes the user and then calls `findMembers()` with the current offset. If the removed user was the only member on the current page (for example 51 members at offset 50), the new total becomes 50 but the request still uses offset 50, so the reload returns an empty page and the UI stays on an invalid blank page. Adjust the offset when it reaches or exceeds the new `user_count` after deletion.

findings.title: Username input is not cleared after adding members or switching groups
findings.body: `usernames` is state on the singleton admin group controller and is not reset after `addMembers` or when `setupController` switches to another group. After adding users to group A, selecting group B leaves the old usernames in the selector; clicking Add again can add those stale users to group B unintentionally. Clear the property after each add and when the model changes (the existing TODO acknowledges this).

findings.title: Creating a group ignores the selected alias level
findings.body: The client’s `Group.asJSON()` sends `alias_level` when creating a group, and the admin template exposes the alias selector for new groups, but `create` only assigns `name` and `visible`. A newly created group therefore silently loses the selected alias level and falls back to the database default. Assign `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i` when present.

findings.title: Public members endpoint response shape is a breaking change
findings.body: `/groups/:group_id/members.json` previously returned a JSON array of users; it now returns an object of the form `{members: [...], meta: {...}}`. The in-repo JavaScript client was updated, but any plugin, mobile app, or external consumer expecting the old array will break. If this endpoint is part of the public API, either maintain backward compatibility or introduce a versioned/new endpoint.

findings.title: remove_member test uses PUT despite the route being DELETE
findings.body: The actual route for removing a member is `DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members`, but the test invokes `xhr :put, :remove_member`. Controller specs bypass routing, so this can pass even if the DELETE route is missing or the PUT route actually maps to `add_members` in production. Use `xhr :delete` to exercise the real contract.
